hydrogen-electrolyser-grid-v1.label: Grid-related electrolyser electricity demand
hydrogen-electrolyser-grid-v1.formula: capacity MWel × 8.76 GWh/MW-year × capacity factor × grid share

sources.basis: IEA analysis uses 3,000–4,000 electrolyser full-load hours for 2019 and 2,000–3,000 for 2050 in the cited case.
NREL evaluates 50% and 90% average electrolyser capacity-factor cases.

hydrogen-electrolyser-grid-v1.limitations: Grid-share ranges are Wattlas analyst assumptions because the project database classifies electricity supply but does not report an hourly grid share. Dedicated-renewable and nuclear projects are excluded from grid demand.

steel-eaf-electricity-v1.label: Electric-arc-furnace electricity demand
steel-eaf-electricity-v1.formula: capacity kt/year × electricity intensity MWh/tonne = GWh/year

sources.basis: DOE reports modern EAF values as low as 300 kWh/t, an average of 436 kWh/t raw steel, and 770 kWh/t shipped steel including auxiliary equipment.

steel-eaf-electricity-v1.limitations: The range represents EAF and associated plant electricity. Blast-furnace and BOF thermal energy is excluded. DRI is retained as context unless its electrical pathway is explicit.

cement-electricity-v1.label: Cement plant electricity demand
cement-electricity-v1.formula: capacity Mt/year × 1,000 × electricity intensity MWh/tonne = GWh/year

sources.publisher: IEA Energy Technology Systems Analysis Programme
sources.basis: The technology brief reports 90–150 kWh/t electricity use and a 111 kWh/t global average.
IEA publishes regional electricity intensity evidence in kWh per tonne of cement.

cement-electricity-v1.limitations: This method estimates electrical grinding and plant auxiliaries. It does not convert kiln thermal fuel into electricity.
